doc.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023

title: Ford Super Bowl commercial with the wrong tape
summary: He was sent the wrong film for a 20 minute Ford project for Elliott Lawrence and recorded the correct parts, then the rest later.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Oh the other car crash session was for Elliott Lawrence where it was a Ford commercial for a Super Bowl and it was 20 minutes long, I think six films of four minutes © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-

interspersed through the thing. And the Monday we were recording with the symphony orchestra. On the Friday afternoon the engineer — the assistant editor phoned me, sorry not the engineer. And he said, “I think you’ve been sent the wrong tape.” So I had to look at it and what he said was — not the right tape — he was right, it was the wrong tape. And I said, “Well how am I supposed to write?” He said, “Well I’ve just been fired so I can’t help you.” So obviously he’d done it in revenge because the guy had, you know the main editor had fired him. He gave me a phone number for the head of Ford or something like that, where the producer was spending the weekend in the Catskills. So I telephoned from London to the Catskills to say I think I’ve got the wrong, you sent me the wrong tape. And the guy was obviously sitting with the boss so he was going, “Oh, no problem at all.” I go, “Yes there is a problem, I can’t write because I’ve got the wrong — I haven’t got any sync points. “Yes well that’s great. We look forward to hearing it on Monday.” I go, “No you don’t understand, I can’t do it.” And he’s covering the phone. Anyway he hangs up and in comes Elliott Lawrence with the guy from the agency and I rang him and said, “Elliott we’ve got a big problem, you know we can’t really do it because it’s all wrong.” And he said, “Well a couple of them are right so just do them.” Okay so we get to the studio and we do the ones that are correct. And I got to the control room and there’s the boss of the agency and Elliott Lawrence and they’re going, “Oh this reminds me of the time we did the so-and-so commercial and they sent the wrong film, ha-ha-ha- ha.” “And what about the time this happened ha-ha-ha-ha-ha.” And I’m sweating, you know because I couldn’t do it. And they’re laughing it off. And then at the end of the week we got the correct cuts and we did the rest of it, you know and it went on. But oh. I aged about ten years.
